name: streaming-response
purpose: Renders a model's Markdown as it streams in (AI Elements Response / Streamdown), safely. The content is parsed by a small Markdown parser into a tree and rendered with Vue elements — never `v-html` — so raw HTML in model output shows as text, `javascript:`, `data:` and protocol-relative links are dropped (only `http(s)`, `mailto`, `tel`, relative and `#` links survive, checked by the shared `safeHref`), and images render as their alt text. It covers what responses use: paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, inline code, links, lists (nested by indenting an item's lines under it, to any depth), block quotes, GFM tables, rules and fenced code (rendered with `CodeBlock`, copyable). Incomplete Markdown is tolerated while streaming: an unclosed `**` renders bold to the end, an unclosed code fence stays a plain `<pre>` until it closes (no highlighting churn), and a half-written link shows its text only. Text renders at the prose reading size (`.text-body-prose-md`, 16 px on 26 px lines, ChatGPT's answer size) with a full step (`--spacing-md`) between blocks, the plain answer column of a chat. Headings are bold, one step larger than the text, 24 px below the block above and 8 px above their first line: `#` at `.text-heading-md`, every deeper level at `.text-body-lg`. Lists indent 32 px from `sm` (24 px on a phone) with no extra gap between items. Inline code is `.text-label-code-md` (14 px) in medium weight. A fenced code block is a filled `CodeBlock` card with the language and copy in a sticky header, the same while the fence is still open. Numbered citations become `Citation` chips resolved against `sources`: `[1]` one chip with the site's mark and name, and a run of markers (`[1][2]`, `[1] [2]`, `[1, 2]`) one chip with `+1` whose card pages through both sources. A blinking caret marks the end while `streaming`; the region is `aria-busy` until the stream ends.
useWhen: Use StreamingResponse for model Markdown that arrives while it renders; a whole documentation page written in MDX uses DocMarkdown.
Any generated text on a page (an explanation, a summary) that arrives token by token.
avoidWhen: Trusted HTML from your own CMS → render it with your CMS pipeline; this component deliberately renders no HTML.
related: `citation`, `sources` — inline references and the panel that lists every source.
`response-loading` — the loading text before the first token, or a bar where a table is coming.
bestPractices: Pass the accumulated text on every chunk; the parser is cheap and the output is keyed by block.
Keep `streaming` true until the stream closes, then false (removes the caret, highlights an open fence).
Pass the response and its `Sources` the same array, so `[n]` is item `n` in both.
Do not post-process model output into HTML; there is no HTML path.

props.name: content
props.doc: The model's Markdown so far. Parsed into elements, never injected as HTML: raw tags render as text and only http(s), mailto, tel, relative and hash links survive.

props.name: streaming
props.doc: Tokens are still arriving: shows the caret, marks the region busy and keeps an unclosed code fence as plain text until it closes.

props.name: sources
props.doc: Sources the `[n]`, `[n][m]` and `[n, m]` citations in the content resolve against: each becomes a chip with the site's favicon and name that opens a card of the sources it cites.
